root_cause.text: The `ceph_process_folio_batch()` function increments `ceph_wbc->num_ops` to account for a new contiguous write extent before attempting to add a folio to the batch, but fails to decrement it when `move_dirty_folio_in_page_array()` fails due to encrypted file bounce buffer allocation failure, leaving the operation count inconsistent with the actual number of folios added.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a decrement of `ceph_wbc->num_ops` when `move_dirty_folio_in_page_array()` fails and `ceph_wbc->len == 0` (indicating a newly-started but empty extent). The CVE description explicitly states: "if this failed folio is not contiguous with the last folio that did make it into the batch, then ceph_process_folio_batch() has already incremented `ceph_wbc->num_ops`; because it doesn't follow through and add the discontiguous folio to the array, ceph_submit_write()...will panic the kernel" due to the mismatch between `num_ops` and actual contiguous ranges. The fix corrects this off-by-one error by reverting the premature increment when the folio addition fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix operation counter leak by decrementing num_ops when a newly-started contiguous write operation fails before accumulating any data.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check within the error handling block of ceph_process_folio_batch() that decrements ceph_wbc->num_ops when ceph_wbc->len equals 0, placed before the folio_redirty_for_writepage() call.
intent_record.how: When move_dirty_folio_in_page_array() fails and returns an error, the code now checks if a new contiguous write operation was just begun (indicated by len == 0). If so, it decrements the operation counter to undo the increment that occurred when the operation was started, preventing an orphaned empty operation from being tracked.
